## Read and clean data

```{r read_and_clean}

# reading data frame
data_frame <- read.csv("data/data_preprocessed/data.csv")

# removing rows we are not interested in
df_clean <- subset(data_frame, original_sentence != "")
# removing practice trials
df_clean <- subset(df_clean, !is.na(correct_change_answer))

```

## Demographic overview

```{r demographics}

demographics <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(language = first(language),
            age = first(age),
            education = first(education))

demographics

# excluding one participant who answered Danish as first language
# -------------------------------------------------------------
participant_to_exclude1 <- c("l4kkhlaf")
df_clean <- subset(df_clean, !participant %in% participant_to_exclude1)
data_frame <- subset(data_frame, !participant %in% participant_to_exclude1)

```

## Excluding participants whose accuracy is too close to chance level

Here, we check the participants' accuracy on all non-target trials. If this accuracy is at chance level, the participants are excluded from further data analysis, as it is too probable that they have just answered randomly throughout the experiment.

```{r excluding participants}

# making a "correct/incorrect"-column
df_clean$correct_incorrect <- ifelse(
  df_clean$Ychange_Nchange_response == "no" & df_clean$correct_change_answer == "no_change" |
    df_clean$Ychange_Nchange_response == "yes" & df_clean$correct_change_answer == "affix_deletion" & df_clean$response == df_clean$correct_response |
    df_clean$Ychange_Nchange_response == "yes" & df_clean$correct_change_answer == "other_change" & df_clean$response == df_clean$correct_response |
    df_clean$Ychange_Nchange_response == "yes" & df_clean$correct_change_answer == "subject_deletion"& df_clean$response == df_clean$correct_response,
  1, 0)

# looking only at non-target trials
df_non_target <- df_clean %>%
  filter(correct_change_answer != "affix_deletion")

# how many correct does each participant have?
df_correct_count <- df_non_target %>% 
  group_by(participant) %>% 
  summarize(correct_count = sum(correct_incorrect))

# looking at the binomial distribution, we can see that the cutoff point must be 27 incorrect answers (p = 0.05).
# if participants have more than 27 incorrect answers (less than 37 correct), it is too probable that they have answered randomly
# note that this assumes equal 50% guessing probability per trial
dbinom(x=27,size=64,prob=0.5)
dbinom(x=28,size=64,prob=0.5)

# excluding participants that have less than 37 correct
participants_to_exclude2 <- c("4fpy89hk", "pe6om3uq")
df_clean <- subset(df_clean, !participant %in% participants_to_exclude2)
data_frame <- subset(data_frame, !participant %in% participants_to_exclude2)

```

## Excluding participants who spent too long on the experiment

```{r excluding participants 2}

# checking how long they spent on the change detection part of the experiment
df_time_change_detection <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(total_time = max(time_elapsed, na.rm = TRUE)/60000)
df_time_change_detection

# excluding outliers whose total time spent on the change detection part was more than 3 SDs from the mean
mean_time <- mean(df_time_change_detection$total_time)
sd_time <- sd(df_time_change_detection$total_time)
cutoff <- mean_time + 3*sd_time
cutoff

participants_above_cutoff <- ("knkl4dbx")
df_clean <- subset(df_clean, !participant %in% participants_above_cutoff)
data_frame <- subset(data_frame, !participant %in% participants_above_cutoff)

```


## Overview of mean reaction times
Here is an overview of the mean reaction times for the three stages of the trials (initial sentence reading, change detection, localization).

```{r reaction times overview, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

reading_time_first_sentence <- data_frame %>%
  group_by(participant, sentence_id_specific) %>%
  summarise(reading_time_sentence1 = first(rt))
mean_reading_time_first_sentence <- reading_time_first_sentence %>%
  filter(!(sentence_id_specific %in% c("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", NA))) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt_sentence1 = mean(reading_time_sentence1))

change_detection_time <- data_frame %>%
  group_by(participant, sentence_id_specific) %>%
  summarise(change_detection_time = rt[[2]])
mean_change_detection_time <- change_detection_time %>%
  filter(!(sentence_id_specific %in% c("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", NA))) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(mean_change_detection_rt = mean(change_detection_time))

localization_time <- data_frame %>%
  group_by(participant, sentence_id_specific) %>%
  summarise(localization_time = rt[[3]])
mean_localization_time <- localization_time %>%
  filter(!(sentence_id_specific %in% c("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", NA))) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(mean_localization_rt = mean(localization_time))

rt_different_stages <- merge(merge(mean_reading_time_first_sentence, mean_change_detection_time), mean_localization_time)

rt_long <- rt_different_stages %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      mean_rt_sentence1,
      mean_change_detection_rt,
      mean_localization_rt
    ),
    names_to = "stage",
    values_to = "rt"
  )

rt_plot <- ggplot(rt_long, aes(x = "", y = rt)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(stage, c("mean_rt_sentence1", "mean_change_detection_rt", "mean_localization_rt"))) +
  ylim(c(0,11000)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Reaction time (ms)",
    title = "Reaction times across stages"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

rt_plot

ggsave("figures/rt_different_stages.png", plot = rt_plot, width = 9, height = 4)

```

## Discarding individual outlier trials with very long reaction times

We discard trials where the sum of the reaction times on the three stages (initial sentence reading, change detection, change localization) is more than three SDs above the participant's own mean. We do this because very long RTs can indicate that the participant zoned out or did not pay attention to the task.

```{r discarding individual trials with long reaction times}

# get reaction times for all trials
rt_different_stages_full <- merge(merge(reading_time_first_sentence, change_detection_time), localization_time) %>%
  filter(!(sentence_id_specific %in% c("p1", "p2", "p3", "p4", NA))) %>%
  mutate(sum_rt = reading_time_sentence1 + change_detection_time + localization_time)

# calculate participant means and SDs - and merge 
rt_mean_and_SD <- rt_different_stages_full %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(sum_rt),
            sd_rt = sd(sum_rt))
rt_different_stages_full_merged <- merge(rt_different_stages_full, rt_mean_and_SD, by = "participant")

# get outlier trials
rt_outliers <- rt_different_stages_full_merged %>%
  filter(sum_rt > mean_rt + 3 * sd_rt)

# exclude outliers


```


# Comparing accuracy in the lexical and grammatical conditions

First, let's check the localization accuracy: Among the affix deletions that were correctly detected, how many were correctly localized?

```{r localization accuracy}

df_clean_affix <- subset(df_clean, correct_change_answer == "affix_deletion")

# LOCALIZATION
df_clean_correct <- df_clean_affix %>%
  filter(correct_incorrect == 1)

df_clean_correct$localization_correct <- ifelse(
  df_clean_correct$response == df_clean_correct$correct_response, 
  1, 0
)

mean(df_clean_correct$localization_correct)

```

All of them were correctly localized. Therefore, we from now on can focus only on change detection accuracy and not worry about the localization step.

## Model to assess the effect of lexical/grammatical condition on accuracy

```{r model1}

model1_affix_type <- glmer(correct_incorrect ~ affix_type + (1|participant),
                          family = 'binomial',
                          df_clean_affix)

summary(model1_affix_type)

```

A second model which includes affix frequency and length as predictors:

```{r model2}

# read csv containing affix frequencies ad calculate log10 frequency
frequencies <- read.csv("research materials/suffix_frequencies.csv", sep = ";")
frequencies <- frequencies %>%
  mutate(log10freq = log10(frequency))

# merge frequency info with affix data frame
df_clean_affix_merged <- merge(df_clean_affix, frequencies, by.x = "target_affix", by.y = "suffix")

# add length column
df_clean_affix_merged <- df_clean_affix_merged %>%
  mutate(affix_length = nchar(target_affix))

# model which includes frequency and lengt as predictors
model2_affix_type <- glmer(correct_incorrect ~ affix_type + 
                             log10freq + affix_length + (1|participant),
                          family = 'binomial',
                          df_clean_affix_merged)

summary(model2_affix_type)


```

# Post-hoc analyses

## Accuracy by reading speed
We saw that accuracy varied a lot between participants. But how does this relate to individual reading speed? 
Here we plot each participant's mean accuracy on the target trials by that participant's mean reading time for the first sentence in a trial.

```{r accuracy by reading speed}

# get mean reading times for sentence 1
df_rt_sentence1 <- rt_long %>%
  filter(stage == "mean_rt_sentence1")
names(df_rt_sentence1)[names(df_rt_sentence1) == "rt"] <- "mean_rt_sentence1"

# merge with df_clean_affix
df_clean_affix2 <- merge(df_clean_affix, df_rt_sentence1, by = "participant")

# plot mean accuracy
mean_accuracy_and_rt <- df_clean_affix2 %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  summarise(mean_rt_sentence1 = first(mean_rt_sentence1),
            mean_accuracy = mean(correct_incorrect))

# (exclude outlier) MAYBE THIS PERSON SHOULD BE EXCLUDED ENTIRELY EARLIER ON
mean_accuracy_and_rt <- mean_accuracy_and_rt %>%
  filter(participant != "5kqwq452")

mean_accuracy_by_rt_plot <- ggplot(aes(x = mean_rt_sentence1, y = mean_accuracy),
                                   data = mean_accuracy_and_rt) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

mean_accuracy_by_rt_plot

```

There is no clear connection at the participant level between mean reading speed and the accuracy with which one detects affix omissions. 

# Looking at sentence ratings

In part 2 of the experiment, we asked all participants to rate all the target sentences on a scale from "sounds like a beginner Kalaallisut speaker" to "sounds like a native Kalaallisut speaker". Here we take a look at the results of those ratings.

```{r ratings}

# removing rows we are not interested in
df_rating <- subset(data_frame, slider_start != "")

# mean rating by sentence id
rating_by_id <- df_rating %>%
  group_by(sentence_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(rating_response))
rating_by_id

# mean rating by condition
rating_by_condition <- df_rating %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(rating_response))
rating_by_condition

```
